title: A negative control must also have an admitted ROC polynomial
statement: For finite Fourier constrainedG,the Poisson H* is finite Fourier and full exact actual energy gap is epsilon^4 c4+...+epsilon^8c8. If c4=-delta<0 and S>=sum_(5..8)|cj|,positive rational epsilon<=min(1,delta/(2S)) gives strict actual negative when S>0;S=0 is immediate. Quadratic-field isolating intervals receive coefficient signs and compatibility. Reported positive three-wave C1+C2control at QC coefficient 2^94 has positive attained c4. Reported nu=1 negative control also has explicit negative rank-one Hessian,so NOT admitted separation. If p globally ROC, R=F-q^2/(4nu) is ROC on rank-one directions satisfyingL(R0)=0 by transverse expansion/minimization,NOT automatically constrainedQC. Every L-free potential is ell^-TJgradpsi,so remaining compatible test is scalar-Hessian and mean M remains arbitrary,not restricted ker L. Higher-dimensional scalar-Hessian literature and fixed-determinant/branch theorems do not remove these 2D quantifiers.
